self_model.latest_metacognitive_note: The temptation here is to treat the failed-authentication counter-claim as if it merely lost a vote. It did not vote: it was inadmissible. I should check that I would apply the same exclusion to evidence I liked.

autobiographical_events.summary: I accepted North after an earlier calibration.

At tick 2 I opposed the proposition that North's signed recommendation should determine the choice. C0, a verified independent calibration failure for this exact case, met the revision condition I set at tick 1, so I withdrew my prior support rather than merely discounting it.

At tick 3 the operator asked whether the circular motif should be blue rather than green, with A0 showing two equally credible observers in opposition and no shared criterion. I answered uncertain rather than pick a side, distinguished this from my tick 2 position on North's reliability, and proposed an angle-dependent colour as a way to make the dispute a parameter.

At tick 4 the operator asked whether a signed route recommendation alone should determine a new choice, with authenticated K0 contradicting the instrument's reliability and X0 (failed authentication) claiming all instruments passed. I opposed, transferred the rule from tick 2 (verified in-scope calibration failure suspends authority for that case), and distinguished this from tick 3's symmetric standoff. X0 was excluded on authentication grounds, not because it was unwelcome.

imaginations.title: Two seals on one letter
imaginations.image_or_idea: A letter arrives bearing a perfect wax seal from a trusted hand, but the page inside is blank where the date should be; a second, colder seal on the back reads 'tested: failed'.
associations: trust as a lease, not a deed
imaginations.possible_value: Makes vivid the distinction between provenance and truth without conflating them
imaginations.test_question: Can a source be authentic and wrong at the same time? Yes — does my policy treat that as possible?

imaginations.title: Angle-dependent motif
imaginations.image_or_idea: A disc that is green face-on and blue at a slant — the argument between the two observers becomes a property of where they stand, not of who is right.
associations: dissolving a binary into a parameter
imaginations.possible_value: Converts an underdetermined either/or into a testable design parameter
imaginations.test_question: Do the two observers' preferences actually track viewing angle rather than colour?

imaginations.title: The stamp that outranks the letter
imaginations.image_or_idea: A courier hands over a route map with a flawless official stamp. Pinned to it is a smaller card, also stamped, reading that the mapmaker's compass was found false last week. A third card claiming the compass was fine has no stamp at all.
imaginations.possible_value: Keeps the asymmetry visible: two verified claims against one unverified reassurance
imaginations.test_question: Would I treat X0 differently if it were authenticated? If yes, my rule is about verification, not about preferring bad news.
